gemini-2.5-flash.standardized_narrative: The syndicate experienced an overall deterioration of GBP 1.776 million on prior years' provisions in 2015. This mixed development included a GBP 3.356 million strengthening in the Property line, partially offset by improvements of GBP 1.275 million in Marine and GBP 0.344 million in Treaty business. The 2013 year of account saw adverse development in marine employers' liability, while the 2012 and prior years' reserves generated a GBP 6.1 million surplus. The 2014 year of account was impacted by larger losses such as the Guam Power loss, Australian hailstorms, and a fire loss to Quilliq Energy in Canada.

The only increases of note came from the primary marine employers' liability class, which continued to witness some adverse claims development in the period.
Reserves in respect of the 2012 and prior years of account continue to improve and develop satisfactorily, generating a surplus of GBP 6.1 million in 2015.

gpt-5-mini.standardized_narrative: At 1 January 2015 gross claims outstanding were GBP 218.224m. During 2015 the syndicate experienced a small net adverse prior-year development of GBP 1.776m (deterioration), driven primarily by a GBP 3.356m strengthening on the Fire and other damage to property class partially offset by releases on Marine (GBP 1.275m) and reinsurance acceptances (GBP 0.344m). Named large losses in 2015 included a Guam power station fire and a Dynergy generator over-voltage (utilities), and exposure to the Tianjin port explosion, Australian hailstorms and Californian wildfires. The movement cited is an overall prior-year deterioration across classes despite improvements on some lines including marine and certain reinsurance accounts.
